## R Objects

### Scalar objects

```{r}
# Create object "n"
n <- 100

# Print the object in the console:
n
```

### Vectors

```{r}
# generate vector "age":
age <- sample(18:65, n, replace = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Visualize
age # Print object in console
str(age) # Object type, size
class(age) # Object type
dim(age)
ls() # List all objects
```

`AirPassengers` is a dataset that comes built into R: the monthly totals of international airline passengers, in thousands, from January 1949 to December 1960. Stores information in three vectors:

```{r}
# Three vectors with one value per month
passengers <- as.numeric(AirPassengers)
year       <- as.numeric(floor(time(AirPassengers)))
month      <- as.numeric(cycle(AirPassengers))

length(passengers)     # 144
```

```{r}
# Access elements of a vector
passengers[1]          # first element: 112
passengers[1:3]        # elements 1 to 3: 112 118 132
passengers[c(1, 144)]  # first and last: 112 432
```

### From Vectors to Dataframes

A **dataframe** is a two-dimensional object that stores data as a table, with rows and columns:

- Each **row** is one observation (an individual, a month, a country, ...).
- Each **column** is one variable (income, education, number of passengers, ...).

```{tikz}
%| echo: false
%| fig-ext: svg
%| fig-align: center
%| out-width: 65%
%| engine.opts:
%|   dvisvgm.opts: "--no-fonts"
\definecolor{PelloGrayDark}{RGB}{60,60,60}
\definecolor{PelloGray}{RGB}{120,120,120}
\definecolor{PelloGrayLight}{RGB}{235,235,235}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1.7cm, y=0.52cm, font=\footnotesize,
    cell/.style={draw=white, line width=1pt, fill=PelloGrayLight, minimum width=1.7cm, minimum height=0.52cm, inner sep=0pt},
    head/.style={cell, fill=PelloGrayDark, text=white, font=\footnotesize\ttfamily}]
    % header
    \node[head] at (0,0) {year};
    \node[head] at (1,0) {month};
    \node[head] at (2,0) {passengers};
    % rows
    \foreach \r/\v in {1/112, 2/118, 3/132, 4/129, 5/121, 6/135} {
      \node[text=PelloGray] at (-0.75,-\r) {\r};
      \node[cell] at (0,-\r) {1949};
      \node[cell] at (1,-\r) {\r};
      \node[cell] at (2,-\r) {\v};
    }
    % one column = one vector
    \draw[teal, line width=1.2pt, rounded corners=2pt] (1.5,0.5) rectangle (2.5,-6.5);
    \node[teal, align=center] at (2,1.5) {a column is a \textbf{variable}:\\ the vector \texttt{passengers}};
    % one row = one observation
    \draw[red, line width=1.2pt, rounded corners=2pt] (-0.5,-2.5) rectangle (2.5,-3.5);
    \node[red, align=left, anchor=west] at (2.65,-3) {a row is an\\ \textbf{observation}:\\ March 1949};
\end{tikzpicture}
```


Every column of a dataframe is a vector, and all columns have the same length. So if we have several vectors of the same length, where position 1 in each vector refers to the same observation, position 2 to the next one, and so on, we can put them side by side as the columns of a dataframe with `data.frame()`. The three vectors `year`, `month` and `passengers` each have 144 elements, one per month, so together they form a dataframe with 144 rows and 3 columns:

```{r}
# Create a dataset from the three vectors
df_air <- data.frame(year, month, passengers)
dim(df_air)            # 144 rows, 3 columns
```



```{r}
head(df_air)
```

## Inspecting Dataframes

```{r}

data(longley)
class(longley)        # "data.frame"
head(longley)
```

### Selecting Observations, Variables

```r
df$age # Print the age column of df
df[[2]] # Same as previous line
```

```r
# Accessing data through row/column indexes
df[1:3,] # Rows 1 to 3, all columns.
df[,c(1,4)] # All rows, Columns 1 and 4.
df[c(1,25),c(1,3)] # Rows 1 and 25, Columns 1 and 3.
```

```r
df_first_fifty_rows <- df[1:50,]
```

### Logical Operators

```r
# Logical condition vector
index_old_males <- (df$gender == "Male") & (df$age > 50)
table(index_old_males)
```

```r
df_old_males <- df[index_old_males, ]
```

```r
df_old_males <- df[(df$gender == "Male") & (df$age > 50), ]
```

## Functions

```r
# Define the function "square()"

square <- function(x) { return(x^2) }

# Run function on object, store as "result"

result <- square(number)

# Print the result in the console

print(result)
```

```r

df$is_higly_educated <- df$education %in% c("Master", "PhD")
```
